messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: control-plane anomalies detected in ap-south-1 — apiserver latency spike + controller-manager restarts around GPU attach churn. Autoclose: 30m

maria (oncall): seeing 502s from the hosted API, lots of short-lived connections. apiserver p95 jumped to 850ms. controller-manager restarted 3x in last 7m.

jake (sre): same. netstat shows conntrack going up fast when GPU nodes attach. suspect SNAT/conntrack exhaustion.

samir (infra): attaching GPUs triggers device-plugin flurry + kubelet kube-proxy churn. We have a recent kube-proxy iptables tweak in canary.

lena (eng): logs from controlplane node-2:
```
Jun 15 09:12:01 apiserver[1]: long running request: 500ms wait on accept
Jun 15 09:12:03 controller-manager[1]: I0615 09:12:03 leader_election.go:243] failed to renew lease: timed out
Jun 15 09:12:04 etcd[1]: committed wal fsync took 480ms
```

maria (oncall): printing `ss -s` we hit high TCP: connections: 207k established, 90k time_wait, `nf_conntrack` usage 65530/65536.

jake (sre): that conntrack number is the smoking gun. SNAT ports + conntrack entries exhausted -> kube-apiserver backpressure -> leader election fails because renew RPCs get delayed.

samir (infra): also saw kernel dmesg spam about `nf_conntrack: table full`. The GPU attach workflow does a burst of `kubelet` -> `kube-proxy` edits + CNI updates -> ephemeral connections to metadata & attacher.

lena (eng): can we see pattern with the GPU attach window? times line up to 09:11:40-09:12:10 where we had a mass attach in ap-south-1 batch-4.

maria (oncall): mitigation options: 1) increase `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` on controlplane nodes, 2) apply conntrack GC tuning, 3) throttle attach orchestration, 4) temporarily move GPU attach jobs to a different region/zone.

jake (sre): short term I pushed a knob to increase `nf_conntrack_max` to 200k on controlplane-*. Also bumped the SNAT port range on nat-gateway as a stopgap.

samir (infra): I'm throttling the attach job by ~5s jitter between attachments and moving non-critical attaches to a rolling window. Triggered a small-scale pause in the central attach pipeline.

lena (eng): longer term: we should reduce hot-path RPCs during attach. Proposal: batch the mutating calls from device plugin so we don't reprogram iptables for every ephemeral attach. Filing ticket in infra-controlplane backlog.

maria (oncall): quick healthcheck after knobs: apiserver p95 dropped to 120ms, controller-manager leader renews OK, conntrack usage back to 78k and falling.

jake (sre): opened PR to revert the kube-proxy canary iptables rule (https://git.redwood/infra/kube-proxy/pull/124) and added a small runbook note: `runbooks/controlplane/conntrack-gpu-attach.md` — contains steps to increase conntrack, SNAT ports, and the attach-throttle command.

lena (eng): attached snippet we used to inspect conntrack counts:
```
# on controlplane
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
ss -s
watch -n1 'cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_count'
```

maria (oncall): FYI we also saw a tiny spike in etcd commit latency during the window. I captured gc/IO traces, but it's secondary to the conntrack problem.

samir (infra): noted. I scheduled a follow-up to review NAT autoscaling and to make SNAT port range autoscale faster during attach storms.

infra-bot: INCIDENT: resolved — control-plane flapping stabilized after conntrack increase + attach throttling. Monitoring for 60m.

maria (oncall): follow-ups:
- add guardrails to attach pipeline (throttle + jitter)
- add conntrack health alert (rate of entries per minute)
- evaluate device-plugin batching (lena owns)
- consider controlplane ephemeral NAT autoscale (samir owns)

jake (sre): I'll add the `leader-election` metric alert to page earlier if renews > 2 in 5m.

lena (eng): creating the batching RFC now.

maria (oncall): thanks team. tagging @oncall-rotation for visibility :thumbsup:
